Marathon Petroleum has fallen about 2% over the past week, declining modestly again today as oil prices stabilized after spiking on geopolitical tensions. Brent crude reached $116 last week on escalating Middle East conflict rhetoric and Houthi attacks on energy infrastructure, but those gains have since cooled—U.S. oil is now trading around $108, down from the recent highs. For refiners like MPC, this price pullback matters: they profit most when crude is cheap relative to finished products like gasoline and diesel, and when demand is strong. Right now, refineries are running at a healthy 93.4% capacity and fuel inventories remain moderate, but the loss of the crude-price spike removes one of the bullish catalysts that pushed the stock higher earlier in the month.

The broader pattern here is that energy stocks and refiners tend to ride geopolitical risk premiums upward, then sell off when those risks feel less acute—even if the underlying tensions haven't fully resolved. The Iran-related headlines that drove oil to six-month highs a few days ago have faded from the immediate news cycle, and without fresh escalation, traders are rotating out of the trade.
